page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-32 is a general-purpose server instance powered by the arm64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor model running at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance profiles across memory and multi-threaded operations. The instance achieves top-tier status in Passmark memory scores and database operations, alongside a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 22619.0. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 3959.51 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 161.74 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1961.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1819.29. Multi-threaded decompression via bzip3 reaches 391.36 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations sustain 68.8 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4a-standard-32 leverages the ARM Neoverse-V2 architecture to deliver high resource density and strong multi-core throughput without the premium associated with traditional x86 architectures. The absence of bundled local storage and GPU accelerators keeps the hardware profile streamlined for compute-heavy and memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe drives. This server is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and medium-scale language model inference tasks.
